title: Poll: Le Pen begins presidential campaign in strongest position ever amid worried, angry electorate
subhed: In France's polarized political landscape, Marine Le Pen of the far-right Rassemblement National is enjoying unprecedented support, and radical left candidate Jean-Luc Mélenchon is building a strong base. Wide open for other candidates, the race is drawing significant interest from voters concerned about the future, Le Monde's first poll shows.

Political scientist Julia Reuschenbach: 'I do not see Chancellor Friedrich Merz resigning'
subhed: Following the Alternative for Germany (AfD) victory in Saxony-Anhalt on September 6, pressure is mounting on Chancellor Friedrich Merz's party, the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), to ease its policy of excluding the far right. Doing so would be a strategic mistake, says political scientist Julia Reuschenbach, who argues that the AfD's goal is to destroy the CDU.

title: Scottish, Welsh, Northern Irish parties to hold independence summit
subhed: The leaders of the separatist parties will hold rare talks on Monday with the aim of advancing their campaigns to break away from Britain. The meeting comes days after US President Donald Trump said he would back a united Ireland – a scenario British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has ruled out.

title: Trump seeks to play peacemaker in a divided Libya
subhed: After 15 years of keeping a low profile on Libya, Washington now wants to reconcile the rival authorities in the country's east and west by brokering a power-sharing agreement negotiated among a handful of local warlords. Far from calming the nation, this initiative has triggered a frantic reshuffling of power dynamics and exposed the fragility of alliances on both sides.
